answer: Each Ember Cartographer node stamps every task with an opal‑colored proof‑of‑unique‑work token, derived from a cryptographic hash of the agent’s computational voyage and a secret umber‑seed that only the genuine processor knows. When a new result is submitted, the ledger rejects any output whose hash matches a previously recorded token within a tolerance window, forcing a Sybil attacker to generate entirely novel work for each forged identity, which costs linear compute and proportional stake for every duplicate.
